conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here because of chest pain. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it started a few days ago. At first it only came with walking, but then it lasted longer. Yesterday it went up into my neck and jaw.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Today it didn’t go away with rest. I was sweating, nauseous. It felt different from my last heart attack—no arm numbness this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You’ve had stents before, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, one in the LAD artery a while back. I haven’t been taking my meds though—lost them when I was moving around.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. Not taking Plavix or aspirin increases your risk. We’ve started you on aspirin, Plavix, and a heparin drip. We also restarted your metoprolol, lisinopril, and statin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. The pain’s better now, but I’ve been feeling shaky and anxious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your EKG and blood tests. No signs of a heart attack—troponins are normal. But your echo showed new wall motion issues in the heart, possibly from reduced blood flow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not blocked again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re concerned a stent might be partially blocked, but since your symptoms improved and tests aren’t showing acute changes, we’ll manage with meds for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your repeat blood tests are stable. But you mentioned last night you’ve been using heroin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah… I didn’t want to say before. I’ve been using about 2 grams a day. I’m feeling withdrawal—sweating, restless, can’t sleep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That explains some symptoms. We’re giving you clonidine and Ativan to help. Social work can help find a detox program.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I want to get clean. But I don’t want to stay here waiting. I’ll find a bed myself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We understand. But it’s risky to leave without a plan. Your heart function is reduced—about 40-45% ejection fraction—and stopping meds could lead to another event.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. I’ll take the meds this time. And I’ll call the detox centers you gave me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re discharging you with a 30-day supply of all your heart meds—Plavix, aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, pravastatin. Also, your albuterol inhaler and citalopram.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Aspirin’s 325 mg now? Wasn’t it 81 before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re increasing it temporarily to reduce clotting risk. Go back to 81 mg daily after a few weeks unless your cardiologist says otherwise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I should follow up with my cardiologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, within a week. Also, weigh yourself daily. If you gain more than 3 pounds in a day, call your doctor—it could mean fluid buildup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ll try to stay on track this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you a list of resources for housing and addiction support. Please use them. Your health depends on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for not giving up on me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We care about your recovery. Take care, and please follow up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do my best.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to leave. Nurse will give you your prescriptions and instructions.
